correctness.rationale: The two six-vertex trees have all 720 equally likely orders exhaustively evaluated. Both direct first-fit permutation enumeration and an independently coded partial-state DP give exactly 350 versus 390 total appearances in colours at least 3, yielding means 397/72 and 131/24. Pruefer sequences cover every labelled tree through five vertices, and all their vertex orders prove none gives a smaller expectation than its path. The code was executed and all exact assertions passed; this is a finite, fully exhaustive proof, not simulation.

value.rationale: The published arXiv:1907.07216 Section 9 explicitly asks whether paths minimize the first two random greedy colour classes on trees. A fully exact, minimum-order six-vertex counterexample resolves the universal yes/no question and delineates a nontrivial boundary of a known path extremality theorem. The result is not valuable only because it is computed: it supplies a structurally motivated obstruction to a proposed extension.
